The 11,851 Plant rows with decimal confidence are positive and negative combined. There are 7,081 verified Plant-absent rows, with 7,000 eligible after conflicts. The publisher's official class hierarchy supports inference downwards from a verified Plant absence. A positive descendant or any vegetation box overrides eligibility as a negative. Missing labels and negative descendant labels alone do not establish Plant absence.

The largest individual non-depiction vegetation box sets positive size. Group-of boxes can cover gaps between plants, so they do not set size. Verified positives with no usable boxes remain in the cohort.
Overall recall is for the sampled cohort with small photos oversampled. The current SegFormer ranker orders all scores and has no rejection threshold.
Only 202 held-out and 231 development positives qualify as small. Full runs include all.

Connected vegetation pixels can merge several plants or split a single plant. Non-crowd potted plant polygon instances are scored separately.
IoU and coverage use the best single proposal per truth region, ignoring void outside the truth. The same proposal can recover more than one region.
The non-vegetation diagnostic counts labelled background over each whole proposal, including void in its denominator. It is a lower bound on the share of background proposals.
Wilson intervals treat pixels, regions or proposals as independent. Their spatial and image-level dependence makes these intervals optimistic.

Only red weed and green crop pixels are assessed positives. Black pixels are unlabelled, never absent. No precision, false alarms or species identity is measured.
Sparse human plant/part polygons were intersected with the publisher NDVI/Otsu vegetation mask. Algorithmic boundaries are not dense human ground truth.
Coverage is computed per positive image/category; Wilson trials are images, not spatially dependent pixels. Category masks with no positive pixels are skipped.
False-colour Red/Near-Infrared/Red imagery; natural-RGB transfer is limited. Noncommercial research only. Pretraining overlap remains unknown.
Historical CWFID results used SAM2 and all 60 photos; this check uses default SAM3 and 20 nonoverlapping publisher test photos, so the headline is not comparable.

limits: Already inspected during development; the fixed 64-image publisher validation subset is not a fresh held-out cohort. No parameters were tuned in this port.
Source semantics: 0 background, 1 crop, 2 weed, 3 partial crop, 4 partial weed. The website repeats partial-crop for ID 4; the publisher devkit confirms partial weed.
SAM3 is class-agnostic: crop/weed strata measure localization, not semantic recognition. These labels cannot measure weed-species identity.
Instance IDs are scoped by crop/weed group; partial plants are included. Foreground without an instance ID contributes only to foreground coverage.
One-to-one maximum-cardinality mask IoU matching at 0.5. Instance Wilson intervals ignore dependence within images; image-coverage intervals use one trial per image.
The archive says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; website/devkit say CC BY-SA 4.0. Retain private noncommercial research handling. Pretraining overlap is unknown.

Conditional identification excludes localization misses; localized_and_identified keeps every labelled box in the denominator. Image-species pairs count each taxon once per photo. Both aggregation policies are descriptive development comparisons.

BioClipClassifier uses a fixed NZ watchlist vocabulary with none of the five ImageWeeds taxa; it cannot measure their species identity. PlantCLEF uses its complete vocabulary. Scores are uncalibrated, not presence probabilities.

limits: The publisher labels the photographed subject. A different labelled subject establishes that a watchlist suggestion is wrong for that subject, while the rest of the frame is unannotated. These rates do not establish scene-level target absence or false alarms.

The pipeline watchlist is Clematis vitalba, Cortaderia selloana and Ulex europaeus. Cytisus scoparius is a declared lookalike. Cortaderia jubata is same genus, and Cytisus proliferus, Genista species and Leptospermum laevigatum are outside the declared lookalike set. Austroderia richardii qualifies via the genus-level declaration.
iNat2021 validation lacks Kunzea, Austroderia fulvida, Austroderia toetoe, Clematis forsteri and Clematis foetida.

There are ten publisher validation photos per species before the source-ID split. Held-out per-species estimates are small, and the species-balanced cohort does not represent deployment prevalence or the composition of New Zealand scenes.
BioCLIP 2 TreeOfLife-200M includes GBIF images from iNaturalist. Undetected overlap may make these estimates optimistic. PlantCLEF uses mostly Pl@ntNet with a GBIF supplement.
The benchmark covers target identification and suggestions. Species outside the fixed BioCLIP prompt vocabulary cannot be identified by that classifier.
Publisher terms allow non-commercial research and education. Images must not be redistributed.

PlantCLEF training metadata (1,408,033 rows) lists Clematis vitalba (plantnet, 527), Cortaderia selloana (plantnet, 457), Ulex europaeus (plantnet, 503). It contains 254,653 rows linking to iNaturalist records or photos and 0 direct filename matches to iNat2021 plant validation images. The val export uses opaque UUID filenames and has no original iNaturalist photo or observation IDs. Direct ID overlap and re-encoded duplicate images remain unverified.
